title: Proportional Reserve Quotas with Graceful Shared-Fallback for Dedicated
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD for introducing proportionally-sized reserved quotas per tenant with an adaptive shared fallback reservoir and deterministic graceful degradation behavior. Targets Dedicated customers who need stronger isolation guarantees but want predictable utilization and burstability. This feature combines deterministic minimums, proportional watermarks, and an FX-based fallback pool that is drain-prioritized by tenant criticality.
background: Current Dedicated reservations are rigid (fixed slot counts) or fully soft (best-effort burst). Customers request predictable isolation for baseline traffic while retaining low-cost burst for spiky workloads. Existing solutions either waste capacity or allow noisy neighbors to starve other tenants. We propose proportional reservation quotas (PRQ) which reserve a tenant's minimum fraction of a capacity pool while enabling controlled burst against a shared fallback reservoir with eviction and fallback policies tied to entitlement tiers.
goals: Provide deterministic minimum capacity guarantees expressed as proportional quotas rather than absolute slots
Allow safe, auditable burst behavior by routing overflow into a shared fallback reservoir with clear QoS rules
Minimize unused capacity compared to fixed over-provisioning models
Expose clear controls in Console for tenants and platform admins to configure proportion, burst budget, and fallback priorities
Ensure graceful degradation with measurable SLOs and clear rollback paths
scope_in: Server-side quota enforcement and admission control changes in Dedicated admission controller
Shared fallback reservoir implementation with draining priorities
Console UI: per-tenant proportion slider, burst budget and fallback priority selector
API: new reservation config fields (proportion_min, burst_budget_sec, fallback_priority, preemption_window_ms)
Runtime metrics & dashboards: per-tenant reserved_fraction, fallback_usage, preemptions, failover_count
scope_out: Billing model changes for proportional reservations (handled by a follow-up pricing project)
Private on-prem bundling changes (may require separate validation)
Model-level per-route QoS within a tenant (future work)
requirements: Customers must be able to set a proportional minimum (0.0 - 1.0) per reserved pool; the system enforces floor and ceiling rules
When aggregate demand exceeds capacity, preemption must follow fallback_priority and within-priority fairness semantics
Fallback reservoir serves bursts up to a configurable global burst headroom; usage is tracked and exposable via Console and API
Preemption notifications (webhook/console) are emitted when fallback consumption leads to tenant eviction from fallback pool
Safe defaults: new tenants default to proportion_min=0.05 (5%) and fallback_priority=standard; admins can opt into stricter isolation
constraints: Must support rollout without downtime for existing Dedicated customers
Changes should not increase steady-state median latency by >5% for normal traffic per runtime perf QA
Implementation must integrate with current autoscaler and not duplicate compute accounting state where possible
Security: reservation metadata must be auditable and require RBAC to change
success_metrics: Reduction in unused reserved capacity compared to fixed-slot baseline by >=12% for pilot customers
Percent of burst requests served from fallback reservoir >= 70% during controlled spikes without violating SLAs
Observed preemption events with consumer-visible notification <= 1 per 100k requests in steady state
Console adoption: 30% of pilot tenants adjust their proportion_min within 30 days
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) internal dogfood cluster (2 weeks) to validate correctness and metrics emission; 2) opt-in beta for 5 pilot tenants with varying load patterns (4 weeks); 3) tiered rollout to all Dedicated customers where proportion_min can be enabled as a target default (8 weeks). Beta includes tight monitoring and a kill-switch to revert to existing reservation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: API: create/update reservation config accepts proportion_min and persists configuration; GET returns applied values
Admission controller: correctly computes per-tenant guaranteed capacity by floor(capacity_pool * proportion_min) and enforces it under normal load
Fallback reservoir: admits overflow requests up to global burst budget and records fallback_usage metric per tenant
Preemption behavior: when global capacity exhausted, eviction order follows fallback_priority; within a priority, evict the tenant with highest fallback_consumption_ratio first
Telemetry: per-tenant metrics (reserved_fraction, fallback_usage, preemptions, failover_count) are present in Console and Prometheus with retention of 90 days
UI: Console shows proportion_min slider, burst budget estimator, and simulated impact preview before apply
Performance: median p50 latency for affected endpoints increases <=5% in rollout testing, and p95 latency degradation limited to <=10% under stress tests
Security: only users with 'capacity:write' role can change reservation settings; all changes produce audit events in the audit log
dependencies: ENG-40211 (Admission controller refactor): required to compute soft guarantees atomically
ENG-41890 (Shared reservoir storage): allocate a durable counter and tracking for fallback usage
ENG-42902 (Console UX primitives): slider and simulation components
PM-56001 (Pricing alignment): coordination for future billing changes
notes: 2025-10-04: Initial scoping meeting; engineering flagged need for atomic counters to avoid race between autoscaler and admission controller.
2025-10-07: Design feedback — make fallback_priority orthogonal to subscription tier so admins can manually raise/lower priority for test tenants.
2025-10-09: Trade-off: tighter isolation reduces multiplexing efficiency. Agreed default proportion_min=5% to balance utilization and predictability.
2025-10-12: Security review requested; audit schema added to ensure changes are logged with old/new values.
2025-10-14: Updated acceptance criteria to include simulated UI preview; added preemption notification webhook requirement per CS request.
